- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — consider slight upward correction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to prevent overshoot.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., after 80+ drop), model tends to underestimate recovery — adjust forecast upward slightly.  
- If history shows volatility and sentiment is neutral, forecast should be more conservative — avoid smooth linear trends.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from forecast mean, check sentiment history for recent spikes — adjust for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- If sentiment history has multiple 0.00 entries, model may be underfitting — add small upward bias to avoid prolonged flat forecasts.
